leading cause of maternal death in the US
: uterus unable to contract to stop the bleed
– to the cervix, perineum or vagina, uterine rupture, lacerations
rapid or prolonged labor, overdistended uterus, C-section, anesthesia, retained placenta
U/S may detect bleed source or retained prod of conception
stage of labor incl oxytocin infusion, gentle cord traction, & uterine massage
: assessment of hemodynamic stability, 2 large-bore IV catheters, rapid infusion of fluids
•early infusion of PRBCs – if ≥4 units/1hr or 10/12-24hrs → FFP & random donor PLT in 1:1:1 ratio
bimanual uterine massage & compress = first line tx
: uterine compress sutures (B-lynch), sequential a. ligation, selective arterial embolization, hysterectomy
: RDS, coagulopathy, shock, loss of fertility, pituitary necrosis (Sheehan syndrome)
the pituitary gland = enlrg during preg which makes it particulary prone to infarct from hypovolemia
ischemia can cause damage to the pituitary gland, impacting the secretion of one or more pituitary hormones
failure to lactate & amenorrhea or oligomenorrhea
Pts w/ PPH who remain hypotensive after the bleed = controlled & vol = corrected should be empirically treated for AI
*The pt can be evaluated for other hormone deficiencies 4-6wks postpartum
